launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.address: 233 South Civic Center Drive, Columbus, OH 43215
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.summary: A connected downtown riverfront of parks, promenades, bridges, fountains, lawns, public art and trails along the Scioto River.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.hours: Bicentennial Park and the Promenade are open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. The fountain, restrooms, events and reservable spaces keep shorter or seasonal schedules.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.parking: The official visitor guide points to downtown parking garages, surface lots and metered street spaces. Event and festival closures can change the closest approach.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.arrival: The Scioto Mile spans more than 175 acres from the Arena District to the Whittier Peninsula, so choose a named park or attraction before parking. The Promenade address is 233 Civic Center Drive.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.restrooms: Permanent accessible restrooms are near the fountain; summer restrooms and changing facilities are also listed at Bicentennial Park and Dorrian Green. The operator does not promise the seasonal facilities year-round.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.cost: The parks and fountains are free and open to the public. Parking, concessions, reservations and ticketed events cost separately.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.accessibility: The operator lists accessible parking, two loading zones, permanent accessible restrooms and accessible routes to the stage lawn, while warning that the 175-acre riverfront includes mixed terrain and long distances.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.dogs: Dogs are welcome on leash, but the official rules keep them out of and away from the fountain. Service animals are allowed throughout the site.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.family: Children eight and younger must be accompanied by an adult in the fountain, and children who are not toilet trained must wear swim diapers. The recirculated fountain water is not drinking water.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.transit: The official directions page recommends arriving by COTA, bicycle or on foot as alternatives to downtown parking.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.need: The interactive fountain is seasonal and can close for weather, sanitation or maintenance. Festivals, construction and high water can affect parts of the riverfront independently.

launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.summary: A 59-acre east-side city park around Franklin Park Conservatory, with a 1.1-mile paved path, cascades, lawns, playground, amphitheater, pond and recreation facilities.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.hours: Franklin Park is open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Franklin Park Conservatory is separately operated and normally open 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with holiday and special-engagement exceptions.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.parking: City parking lots are off East Broad Street and Franklin Park West. Conservatory visitors can use its free lots A and B and the Wells Barn lot; busy exhibitions and events can fill the closest spaces.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.arrival: Use 1755 East Broad Street for the city park. The separately operated Conservatory is at 1777 East Broad Street, and its visitor entrance and parking are the clearest arrival point for ticketed gardens.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.restrooms: The city park page does not list a general public restroom. Conservatory restrooms are available to visitors during its operating hours, so do not rely on them when the attraction is closed.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.cost: Outdoor city-park grounds are free. Conservatory admission is ticketed; as checked, general prices including the cultural-arts fee are $25.20 for adults, $21 for seniors, $17.33 for children ages 3–12, and $4 with qualifying SNAP, EBT, WIC or Medicaid identification.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.accessibility: The city lists a 1.1-mile paved path. The Conservatory provides paved approaches, ramps, elevators and a limited number of free wheelchairs, but outdoor lawn and garden surfaces vary.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.dogs: In city park areas, animals must be securely leashed or under direct control and waste must be removed. The Conservatory allows service animals only, including in its outdoor gardens.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.family: The free city park includes a playground and lawns. The Children's Garden belongs to the paid Conservatory visit, and its Sandstone Creek water feature has been closed since June 17, 2026.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.transit: The Conservatory identifies COTA Route 10 service along East Broad Street near the site.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.need: The Cascades have been closed since June 23, 2026 because of a leak in the lower pond. At the Conservatory, the Palm House, Davis Showhouse and Wolfe Terrace are closed for renovation until fall 2027.

launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.summary: A 32-acre Short North city park with a pond, mature trees, playground, courts, shelterhouse, gazebo, gardens and neighborhood paths.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.hours: Goodale Park is open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. The Shelterhouse is a reservable building with separate rental access Tuesday through Sunday and on holidays.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.parking: City parking lots are off Park Street and Dennison Avenue. Large events and Short North traffic can affect access, so verify event notices before relying on the closest lot.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.arrival: Use 120 West Goodale Street for the park. Select the pond or Shelterhouse before arrival because the park spans several blocks and the official facility map records them as separate destinations.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.restrooms: The Shelterhouse includes restrooms for building users. The city park page does not promise a separate walk-up public restroom, so confirm building or event access before relying on it.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.cost: Ordinary park use is free. Shelterhouse rental starts at $100 per hour for city residents and $120 per hour for nonresidents, with minimum hours and other fees depending on the booking.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.accessibility: The city lists paved paths and describes the Shelterhouse as accessible. Older outdoor paths, turf and pond-edge conditions vary, so that does not establish that every park route is barrier-free.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.dogs: Animals must be securely leashed or under direct control, and handlers must remove waste. Goodale Park is not listed as a city off-leash dog park.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.family: The playground, pond and open lawns support a simple central-city family stop. Keep children back from the open pond edge and verify major-event conditions.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.transit: The official park page links to COTA's trip planner; High Street service is a short walk east of the park.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.need: Large events can transform parking and circulation. The pond is an open water body, and the city does not list Goodale Park among its swimming facilities.

launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.summary: A 23.6-acre German Village community park with a paved loop, stocked pond, amphitheater, community center, playground, courts, gardens and historic Schiller Statue.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.hours: Schiller Park is open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. The Schiller Community Center is normally open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. and closed Saturday and Sunday; programs and holiday schedules can differ.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.parking: The city park page lists a parking lot, and the official facilities layer places the community-center arrival at 1069 Jaeger Street. No general park parking fee is posted; performances, festivals and permitted events can change availability.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.arrival: Use 1069 Jaeger Street for the community center and east-side amenities. Use the City Park Avenue side for Huntington Gardens and the Schiller Statue; the city identifies the statue area as the general public entrance that must remain unobstructed.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.restrooms: The reliable documented restroom opportunity is inside the Schiller Community Center during its staffed hours. The city park page does not promise a separate always-open outdoor restroom.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.cost: The city posts no admission charge for ordinary outdoor park use. Community-center classes, permits, reserved wedding sites and special programs can require registration or fees.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.accessibility: The city documents a 0.8-mile paved path and mapped developed facilities. That does not establish that every lawn, garden bed, pond edge, older curb or amphitheater seating area is barrier-free.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.dogs: Animals must be securely leashed or under direct control and handlers must remove waste. Schiller Park is not one of the city's five designated off-leash dog parks.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.family: The city lists a playground, pond, paved path and sports facilities. Keep children close at the open pond, and confirm posted conditions before relying on the playground during the city's planned improvement cycle.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.transit: The park page links CoGo bike share, and COTA's official trip planner can identify the current bus approach. The east and west sides serve different destinations, so select the community center, pond or statue before routing.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.need: The amphitheater and garden areas can host performances, weddings and volunteer work. The city's long-range program identifies future pond and playground renovation, but planning documents are not closure notices; obey current signs and alerts rather than assuming either feature is closed.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.weather: Check the National Weather Service Columbus forecast for heat, thunderstorms, high wind, snow or ice. The park has exposed lawns, mature trees and an open pond, and individual programs can cancel independently of park hours.

launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.summary: A 149-acre Clintonville regional park with the free Columbus Park of Roses, community center, stocked pond, prairie, playground, courts, fields and Olentangy Trail access.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.hours: Whetstone Park is open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Columbus Park of Roses keeps shorter hours of 7:00 a.m. to dusk year-round, and the community center is normally open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.parking: The park has multiple lots. Park of Roses visitors are directed west on Hollenback Road to free garden parking; step-free ADA parking is at the garden's east end off Roselea Place. Construction and busy bloom-season events can change the closest approach.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.arrival: Use 3923 North High Street for the community center and east-side recreation. For the Park of Roses, enter Whetstone Park on Hollenback Road and continue about one-half mile west; route to a named facility because the grounds cover 149 acres.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.restrooms: The Park of Roses provides portable restrooms at the east end near ADA parking and north of the Shelterhouse. Shelterhouse indoor restrooms are available to event users, and community-center facilities depend on staffed hours.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.cost: Columbus Park of Roses has no admission fee and its visitor parking is free. Ordinary park use is not ticketed; shelterhouse rentals, wedding sites, classes and reserved activities cost separately.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.accessibility: The city documents 1.6 miles of paved park path, and the garden provides step-free ADA parking off Roselea Place. Prairie paths, turf, trail connections and construction areas can have different surfaces or temporary barriers.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.dogs: Animals in city parks must be securely leashed or under direct control and waste must be removed. On the Olentangy greenway, pets must use a leash no longer than six feet; protect formal garden beds.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.family: The park page lists a playground, stocked pond, paved path and gardens, and the city reports a recently added lower-fields playground. Supervise children at the pond and keep them out of planted beds.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.transit: The Park of Roses directs riders to COTA Route 2 on North High Street at Acton Road, followed by about a half-mile walk west on Hollenback Road. The Olentangy Trail provides bicycle access to Whetstone Park.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.need: Peak rose bloom generally runs from mid-June through mid-September. The city lists 2026 path, Hollenback Road, pond-lot and community-center work and warns that schedules depend on contractors and weather, so check signs and the improvements page before relying on the usual route.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.weather: Check the National Weather Service Columbus forecast before a garden, prairie or trail visit. Rose bloom and outdoor comfort vary with heat and rain, and storms, wind, snow or ice can affect paths and programs independently.

launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.summary: A 1,204-acre Metro Park with 100-foot shale bluffs, deep ravines, river overlooks, nature center, natural play, picnic areas and varied trails.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.hours: April 1-September 30: 6:30 a.m.-10:00 p.m. October 1-March 31: 6:30 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Nature Center: 9:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. in summer and 9:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in winter.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.parking: Free lots serve the Nature Center, Big Meadows, Oak Coves, River Bluff and trail areas. Navigate to the exact area rather than the general park pin.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.arrival: Use the Nature Center for exhibits, Big Meadows for playgrounds and natural play, or the named Overlook, Dripping Rock and Scenic River trailheads.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.restrooms: ADA restrooms serve the Nature Center and developed picnic areas; some shelter-area restrooms are seasonal.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.cost: Park admission, parking, trails, nature center and first-come picnic shelters are free. Reservations and programs may vary.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.accessibility: The Nature Center, Scenic River and Sycamore trails and picnic facilities offer accessible options; Overlook and Dripping Rock are hillier gravel routes.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed on designated pet trails and in picnic and parking areas, but not every preserve trail.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.family: Big Meadows combines playgrounds, playfields, picnic shelters and a 15-acre natural play area; the Nature Center is a strong weather backup.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.transit: Regional transit is limited; driving or cycling is practical for most visitors.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.need: The Overlook Trail is a moderate-to-difficult 2.3-mile route to a deck 100 feet above the Olentangy. Stay on trail in the state nature preserve.

launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.summary: A 7,358-acre Metro Park along two scenic rivers with bison pastures, a living-stream nature center, prairies, wetlands, natural play, trails and paddling access.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.hours: April 1-September 30: 6:30 a.m.-10:00 p.m. October 1-March 31: 6:30 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Nature Center: 9:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. in summer and 9:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in winter.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.parking: Free lots are spread among the Nature Center, Indian Ridge, Cedar Ridge, canoe area, Osprey Lake and Pleasant Valley. Select the exact area first.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.arrival: The Nature Center and bison pastures are the simplest first visit. Indian Ridge serves natural play; paddling and southern trail areas use separate entrances.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.restrooms: Restrooms serve the Nature Center and major picnic areas, while remote trails and access points have limited facilities.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.cost: Park, parking, trails, bison viewing and nature center are free. Reservations and organized programs may vary.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.accessibility: The Nature Center and selected greenway and picnic routes are accessible; natural trails, creek banks and prairie surfaces vary.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on designated pet trails and developed areas; keep well away from bison fencing and wildlife.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.family: The living stream in the Nature Center, bison viewing and nine-acre natural play area make a strong family sequence.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.transit: There is little practical public transit to the distributed park entrances; driving is recommended.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.need: Bison roam two enclosed pastures and may be distant or temporarily out of view. Never cross fencing or approach wildlife; bring binoculars.

launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.summary: A reclaimed 182-acre quarry with a 25-foot waterfall, lakes, paved paths, mountain biking, dog park, paddling, sport climbing and reservation-only via ferrata.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.hours: Open year-round from 6:30 a.m. until dark. Programs, climbing access and construction areas may use separate schedules.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.parking: Use 2158 Old Dublin Road for Millikin Falls, 2600 Dublin Road for the north area and mountain biking, or 2319 Quarry Trails Drive for the lake area.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.arrival: Do not use one general pin. Choose Waterfall Entrance, Northern Area or Lake Area before driving; they do not function as one compact lot.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.restrooms: Restrooms and portable facilities are available in developed areas, but coverage varies while the park continues to develop.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.cost: Park, parking, trails, waterfall, dog park and ordinary lake access are free. Via ferrata requires a guided program reservation; climbers provide required gear for sport routes.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.accessibility: The paved North-South Connector includes an ADA boardwalk from Lake Area parking. Waterfall steps, bike routes and climbing areas are not universally accessible.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.dogs: Leashed pets are welcome on designated paths, and a two-acre fenced dog park separates small and large dogs; running water is not guaranteed there.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.family: The waterfall overlook, lakes and paved paths work for general visits. Climbing and mountain-bike areas require age, skill, gear and supervision appropriate to the activity.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.transit: Transit is limited at the separated entrances; driving or cycling is usually simplest.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.need: Via ferrata access is guided and reservation-only, for visitors at least 14, at least five feet tall and 88-265 pounds. The 90-minute route includes elevated cable crossings.
